Healthcare adaptation is named where appropriate, rather than treating every prospective method as FMEA.

metadata.title: Metastatic cutaneous melanoma involving small bowel
metadata.completeCitation: Wong P, Wisneski AD, Tsai KK, Chang TT, Hirose K, Nakakura EK, Daud AI, Maker AV, Corvera CU. Metastatic melanoma to small bowel: metastasectomy is supported in the era of immunotherapy and checkpoint inhibitors. World Journal of Surgical Oncology. 2024;22:77. Published March 11, 2024. doi:10.1186/s12957-024-03335-3. PMID:38468341. Accessed October 7, 2026. Introduction and case-series description used only for occurrence.
metadata.organizationOrJournal: World Journal of Surgical Oncology
metadata.licenseLabel: Actual article states CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/, verified October 7, 2026; it also identifies US-government-work conditions with possible foreign protection. Conservative CC BY attribution retained. Original occurrence facts only; no source figures, patient data, tables or prose reproduced.
metadata.reuseNotes: Original factual synthesis only; no source prose, tables, figures, charts, or algorithms reproduced.
metadata.authorityAssessment: 2024 single-institution fifteen-patient retrospective surgical case series. Introduction and case description verify that cutaneous melanoma can spread to small bowel. The selected cohort cannot establish population prevalence, most-common-primary rankings or benefit of surgery. No therapy recommendation, survival estimate, exact interval, histologic diagnostic shortcut or postoperative protocol is inferred.

metadata.title: WSES esophageal emergencies guideline: foreign bodies
metadata.completeCitation: Chirica M, Kelly MD, Siboni S, Aiolfi A, Riva CG, Asti E, Ferrari D, Leppäniemi A, ten Broek RPG, Brichon PY, Kluger Y, Fraga GP, Frey G, Andreollo NA, Coccolini F, Frattini C, Moore EE, Chiara O, Di Saverio S, Sartelli M, Weber D, Ansaloni L, Biffl W, Corte H, Wani I, Baiocchi G, Cattan P, Catena F, Bonavina L. Esophageal emergencies: WSES guidelines. World Journal of Emergency Surgery. 2019;14:26. Published May 31, 2019. doi:10.1186/s13017-019-0245-2. PMID:31164915. Accessed October 7, 2026.
metadata.organizationOrJournal: World Society of Emergency Surgery; World Journal of Emergency Surgery
metadata.licenseLabel: Article-specific CC BY 4.0 verified in the actual article October 7, 2026, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Attribution to authors and original guideline recorded. Original narrow clinical facts only; no source recommendation table, algorithm, illustration or prose adapted.
metadata.reuseNotes: Original factual synthesis only; no source prose, tables, figures, charts, or algorithms reproduced.
metadata.authorityAssessment: 2019 WSES guideline remains listed by the current official WSES guideline index, checked October 7, 2026; no newer named WSES esophageal update was found. Foreign-body questions on imaging and endoscopy directly support radiographic bone limitations, persistent-symptom evaluation despite negative films and emergent sharp-esophageal-object removal. ESGE independently agrees, but both are older guidelines with largely low-quality underlying evidence. No numeric diagnostic performance, removal deadline or extraction technique is imported.

metadata.title: Refeeding physiology in a neurocritical cohort report
metadata.completeCitation: Zhang W, Zhang S-X, Chen S-F, Yu T, Tang Y. Development and validation of risk prediction model for refeeding syndrome in neurocritical patients. Frontiers in Nutrition. 2023;10:1083483. Published February 15, 2023. doi:10.3389/fnut.2023.1083483. Accessed October 7, 2026. Mechanism background in Introduction.
metadata.organizationOrJournal: Frontiers in Nutrition
metadata.licenseLabel: Article-specific CC BY 4.0 verified in the actual publisher copyright notice October 7, 2026, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Authors and original article credited here. Claims/cards independently synthesize underlying physiology; no prose, predictive model, table or figure adapted.
metadata.reuseNotes: Original factual synthesis only; no source prose, tables, figures, charts, or algorithms reproduced.
metadata.authorityAssessment: 2023 observational neurocritical-care cohort. Its Introduction independently describes the insulin-associated intracellular phosphate uptake and catabolic-to-anabolic transition after feeding. Those stable background mechanisms alone are used; the cohort's risk model, incidence, thresholds and neurocritical-care management are not generalized to clinic patients. Not independent evidence for thiamine timing or efficacy.

metadata.statement: A positive hCG result establishes evidence of pregnancy but does not by itself establish its location; clinical assessment and appropriate ultrasonography are needed to evaluate a suspected ectopic pregnancy.
metadata.limitation: No hCG discriminatory value, definitive ultrasound rule, treatment regimen or mandatory test sequence is authored.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults being evaluated for a possible ectopic pregnancy.

metadata.statement: A positive pregnancy test with compatible pelvic pain or abnormal vaginal bleeding raises concern for an ectopic pregnancy and requires prompt specialist-capable assessment even when the initial circulation is stable.
metadata.limitation: Current guideline corroborated by independent government symptom guidance. This is suspicion requiring urgent evaluation, not a definitive ectopic diagnosis or an onsite treatment recommendation. The NHS page's displayed review is overdue. Escalating pain, faintness or other deterioration requires emergency assessment without a routine testing wait.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Symptomatic adults with a positive pregnancy test and an unestablished pregnancy location.

metadata.statement: For a persistent esophageal foreign body requiring removal, therapeutic endoscopy is the initial approach when the supplied assessment has not identified a complication or circumstance requiring an operation.
metadata.limitation: WSES 2019 endoscopy and surgical-indication sections directly support initial endoscopic care and separately identify operative indications. Sole direct source for this narrow comparator boundary. No extraction technique, universal avoidance of surgery, patient self-treatment or clinic procedure is taught.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with a confirmed retained esophageal foreign body and no supplied operative complication.

metadata.statement: Some swallowed fish or chicken bones are not readily visible on plain radiographs, so a negative film does not exclude a retained bone.
metadata.limitation: Direct concordant WSES 2019 imaging guidance and official ESGE 2016 PDF page 3. The older guidelines remain on current official indexes; underlying diagnostic evidence has limitations. No exact sensitivity, false-negative proportion, blanket plain-film-first rule or claim that every bone is radiolucent.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Symptomatic adults reporting swallowed fish or chicken bone.

metadata.statement: Persistent esophageal symptoms after a suspected swallowed foreign body warrant further specialist evaluation even when plain radiographs are negative.
metadata.limitation: WSES 2019 endoscopy section directly supports evaluation despite negative radiographs; ESGE independently cross-checks the radiographic bone limitation and therapeutic assessment. No complete imaging sequence or numeric removal deadline. Normal breathing does not resolve the supplied esophageal concern; urgent outside assessment is a case disposition rather than new clinic capability.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with ongoing swallowing-related symptoms after suspected sharp-bone ingestion.

metadata.statement: A confirmed sharp-pointed foreign body retained in the esophagus is an indication for emergent therapeutic endoscopic removal.
metadata.limitation: WSES 2019 endoscopy recommendation and ESGE 2016 official PDF page 4 agree. Strong guideline recommendations rely on largely low-quality evidence; age and current index status are recorded. The cases direct emergency hospital care outside the clinic, not a routine timed game EGD, a rescue protocol, extraction technique or a numeric deadline.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with supplied confirmation of a sharp esophageal foreign body.

metadata.statement: A sharp-pointed esophageal foreign body presents a risk of full-thickness esophageal injury, which underlies the need for emergent removal even without complete obstruction.
metadata.limitation: Both guidelines support sharp-object urgency independent of the separate complete-obstruction indication. No exact perforation probability or claim that injury has already occurred. Cases have confirmed esophageal location, normal respiration and no supplied perforation; no onsite treatment or automatic surgery is inferred.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with a confirmed retained sharp esophageal object and preserved breathing.

metadata.statement: Systemic local-anesthetic toxicity can also involve cardiac conduction disturbances and serious ventricular arrhythmias.
metadata.limitation: Targeted ASRA discussion sections 6 and 8 support cardiac involvement. Sole direct source; no ECG cutoffs, frequency, mandatory waveform or treatment protocol is claimed. A supplied compatible exposure is necessary for the case reasoning.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing documented cardiac findings after outside local-anesthetic administration.

metadata.statement: Systemic local-anesthetic toxicity can produce neurologic findings such as altered taste, tinnitus, perioral numbness, confusion and seizures in a compatible exposure context.
metadata.limitation: ASRA educational discussion section 8 is the sole direct recognition source, published 2021. These findings are not individually diagnostic or a required sequence; the cases supply local-anesthetic exposure and a completed outside clinical course. No source vignette or rescue algorithm is reused.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a completed outside-care event after local-anesthetic exposure.

metadata.statement: Cardiovascular manifestations of systemic local-anesthetic toxicity can be the initial presentation, so a preceding neurologic warning sequence is not required.
metadata.limitation: ASRA educational section 8 directly supports possible cardiac-first presentation. This is a recognition limit, not a claim that every perioperative arrhythmia is toxicity or that the supplied event's cause can be established without clinical evaluation.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a completed outside event with documented local-anesthetic exposure.

metadata.statement: Local-anesthetic inhibition of voltage-gated sodium-channel function reduces the sodium current needed for nerve excitation and action-potential conduction.
metadata.limitation: Mechanistic review is the sole direct source for the conduction explanation. No specific concentration, onset, duration, sensory-fiber ranking or irreversible nerve effect is claimed.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Sensory nerve membranes exposed to a conventional local anesthetic.

metadata.statement: Voltage-gated sodium channels are the principal molecular target responsible for the nerve-blocking action of conventional local anesthetics such as lidocaine.
metadata.limitation: Principal mechanism, not a claim that these medicines interact with no other targets. Molecular review and independent government classification; no administration or dose rule.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing local-anesthetic action in sensory nerves.

metadata.statement: A cancer metastasis retains the identity of its established primary cancer; its new anatomic location does not by itself make it a primary cancer of that organ.
metadata.limitation: Current NCI explanation directly supports primary identity and naming after metastatic spread. The cases give a specialist pathology comparison confirming the relationship to a known cutaneous primary. No unknown-primary ranking, diagnosis from one stain, melanoma subtype inference or management decision.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a confirmed metastasis from a supplied known primary.

metadata.statement: Cutaneous melanoma can metastasize to the small bowel.
metadata.limitation: The 2024 retrospective case series directly establishes occurrence, not a population frequency or ranking of primary cancers. No survival, treatment benefit, timing or diagnostic marker threshold is inferred from this selected surgical cohort.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with an established cutaneous melanoma history and a supplied outside small-bowel pathology diagnosis.

metadata.statement: A persistent unexplained lateral neck mass in an adult requires evaluation for malignancy; a cystic appearance in an older adult does not establish a benign developmental cyst.
metadata.limitation: Single independent multidisciplinary guideline directly supports the malignancy/cystic boundary. The cases are adults older than40 with persistent unexplained nonthyroid masses, not a thyroid-nodule, thyroglossal-duct or known benign-cyst objective. No precise duration threshold or definitive cancer diagnosis is inferred.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults older than40 with a persistent unexplained lateral or cystic neck mass.

metadata.statement: Core needle biopsy may be appropriate for selected neck masses when the tissue or ancillary testing needed is not adequately supplied by fine-needle aspiration.
metadata.limitation: Single guideline; core is acknowledged in feedback and is never an incorrect alternative to FNA. The cases do not ask for lymphoma-specific sampling or prescribe open biopsy after a fixed number of attempts.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Specialist-assessed neck masses with technique selection based on pathology requirements.

metadata.statement: Cross-sectional neck imaging characterizes anatomy, whereas cell or tissue sampling supplies the material for a cytological or histological diagnosis of an undiagnosed suspicious neck mass.
metadata.limitation: Single guideline's independently synthesized distinction between imaging and needle-sampling roles. A supplied CT description does not substitute for a tissue specimen; no universal sequence or guaranteed sampling result is claimed.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with an imaged but still undiagnosed suspicious cervical mass.

metadata.statement: After appropriate assessment of an undiagnosed at-risk adult neck mass, fine-needle aspiration is an appropriate initial needle-sampling approach; open incisional or excisional biopsy should not replace the initial needle approach.
metadata.limitation: Single independent guideline. FNA is the best offered needle option, not universally preferable to core biopsy. The game action is specialist referral, not a fabricated local generic-FNA procedure or a complete cancer-workup sequence.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with an assessed, undiagnosed suspicious cervical mass requiring an initial needle sample.

metadata.statement: Contrast-enhanced neck CT can be an appropriate selected cross-sectional study to characterize a nonthyroid/nonparotid neck mass and its cervical anatomy during malignancy evaluation.
metadata.limitation: Society-reviewed2022 patient summary supports CT among appropriate options, corroborated by UK2024 CT/anatomy guidance. Primary ACR2018 narrative/portal was inaccessible and is not used. MRI and ultrasound can also be appropriate; CT is not universally superior or mandatory before FNA. No felt/cannot-felt distinction is used.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a persistent nonpulsatile nonthyroid/nonparotid neck mass and a specialist-selected cross-sectional imaging plan.

metadata.statement: Bending the elbow for prolonged periods or leaning on the inner elbow can provoke symptoms from ulnar compression at the cubital tunnel.
metadata.limitation: Current patient guidance supports provocation, not a guarantee of diagnosis from position alone or a treatment protocol.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with elbow-provoked little/ring-finger paresthesias.

metadata.statement: Carpal tunnel syndrome localizes compression of the median nerve to the carpal tunnel at the wrist.
metadata.limitation: Single federal educational source for foundational anatomy, updated 2018. Supplied clinical clues support localization; no automatic operation, electrodiagnostic test or universal cause of hand tingling is asserted.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied carpal-tunnel pattern or an outside localization report.

metadata.statement: Median-nerve compression at the wrist can produce hand numbness and tingling involving the thumb, index and middle fingers, with nocturnal or wrist-position-provoked symptoms.
metadata.limitation: Only the sourced symptom distribution and wrist/nocturnal context are used. No exact sensory boundary, prevalence, occupational causation or diagnostic certainty from one symptom is claimed.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with characteristic supplied wrist-level median symptoms.

metadata.statement: Cubital tunnel syndrome localizes ulnar-nerve compression to the inner elbow and can produce tingling or numbness in the little and ring fingers.
metadata.limitation: Single current NHS hand-therapy source for the narrow localization. Ulnar symptoms alone do not distinguish every elbow, wrist or proximal lesion; the authored cases supply elbow-localizing findings.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with characteristic supplied elbow-level ulnar findings.

metadata.statement: Rocuronium's neuromuscular blockade does not itself provide unconsciousness or pain relief; adequate anesthesia or sedation is a separate requirement when it is used.
metadata.limitation: Label section 5.4 directly supports this boundary. Absence of movement cannot independently establish adequate anesthesia. Sole direct source; no ASA sedation definitions, awareness incidence or rescue/administration instructions are used.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving patient counseling about neuromuscular blockade.

metadata.statement: Rocuronium is a neuromuscular blocking drug that produces skeletal-muscle relaxation through blockade at the motor end plate.
metadata.limitation: Current label sections 1 and 12.1 are the sole direct source. A qualitative drug-effect classification, not a dose, administration technique, recovery interval or respiratory-management protocol.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing documented rocuronium use in outside anesthesia care.

metadata.statement: Reduced hemoglobin can reduce blood oxygen-carrying content even when the remaining hemoglobin has a normal oxygen saturation, so a normal SpO2 alone does not exclude anemia or establish adequate oxygen content.
metadata.limitation: Qualitative physiological inference from independently verified hemoglobin-carriage and saturation-fraction facts; FDA device background also describes reduced oxygen-carrying ability in anemia. Other determinants of tissue oxygen delivery are not assessed. No numeric content equation, hemoglobin threshold or treatment decision.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with established anemia discussing an outside blood-count result.

metadata.statement: An ordinary pulse-oximeter display can report oxygen saturation and pulse rate, sometimes with signal strength; those displayed values do not provide a hemoglobin concentration.
metadata.limitation: FDA 2025 consumer page is the sole direct source for ordinary clip display fields. Cases explicitly supply those fields only. This does not claim that every specialized multi-parameter device lacks additional functions, and it does not order a new blood test.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults interpreting supplied ordinary pulse-oximeter display values.

metadata.statement: Hemoglobin in red blood cells carries oxygen, and its blood concentration is a separate quantity from the percentage oxygen saturation.
metadata.limitation: NHLBI December 2025 CBC explanation verifies hemoglobin carriage; FDA background verifies saturation's proportional meaning. Original qualitative comparison, without a numeric anemia threshold, race-specific reference range, transfusion indication or claim about cardiac output.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied outside hemoglobin result and saturation reading.

metadata.statement: Pulse-oximeter SpO2 estimates the proportion of hemoglobin oxygen-binding capacity occupied by oxygen, expressed as a percentage.
metadata.limitation: FDA 2024 executive-summary Introduction supplies the hemoglobin-fraction explanation; FDA 2025 consumer page independently confirms the percentage estimate. SpO2 is an estimate with device limitations, not a direct measurement of blood oxygen content or tissue delivery. No formula or fixed normal threshold.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults interpreting an ordinary supplied pulse-oximeter reading.

metadata.statement: A home urine pregnancy test taken early can be negative despite pregnancy, so an early negative home result does not settle pregnancy status when compatible symptoms persist.
metadata.limitation: Single federal test-information source; no exact repeat interval, detection threshold or assay sensitivity is specified.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with a possible early pregnancy and an early negative home test.

metadata.statement: Pregnancy testing for hCG is part of the assessment of reproductive-age pelvic or abdominal pain when pregnancy is possible; menstrual history or reported contraception does not substitute for testing when early-pregnancy complications are suspected.
metadata.limitation: Guideline and independent government test information. The authored task selects testing as part of immediate assessment; it does not postpone urgent care, select a universal urine-versus-serum assay, or diagnose an ectopic pregnancy.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Reproductive-age adults with pelvic/abdominal symptoms and possible pregnancy.

metadata.statement: Hair follicles contain epithelial cells that can contribute to skin-wound re-epithelialization.
metadata.limitation: Mechanistic review and donor-site narrative corroboration. Models do not establish an exact human healing time or imply every epithelial source is interchangeable; the authored donor cases explicitly retain appendages.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Skin wounds with retained epithelial hair-follicle structures.

metadata.statement: After a split-thickness skin harvest, retained epithelial elements of deeper skin appendages at the donor site can regenerate the donor wound's epithelial surface.
metadata.limitation: The historical narrative review is the sole direct donor-site source. Independent hair-follicle mechanistic evidence corroborates epithelial contribution but is not a donor-management guideline. No exact healing interval, harvest depth, guaranteed outcome or full-thickness donor closure rule is asserted.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a partial-thickness skin-graft donor wound with retained appendages.

metadata.statement: A free flap carries its vessels with the transferred tissue, with those vessels reconnected at the recipient site to establish perfusion.
metadata.limitation: Independent sources corroborate free-flap vascular transfer. Being detached during transfer does not make it a skin graft when the supplied record documents vessel reconnection; no onsite microsurgical capability is implied.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a completed outside free-flap reconstruction.

metadata.statement: A skin graft is transferred without its own connected blood supply and depends on the recipient bed for support and subsequent vascularization.
metadata.limitation: Single current peer-reviewed review for the graft definition. No exact stages, timing of vascularization, selection rule or graft-survival guarantee is used.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing documented skin-graft reconstruction.

metadata.statement: A pedicled flap moves tissue while retaining a vascular connection that supplies the transferred tissue.
metadata.limitation: Current review and independent federal fact sheet support the vascular principle. No named flap design, operative instruction or outcome ranking is inferred.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a documented pedicled tissue transfer.

metadata.statement: The graft-versus-flap distinction concerns transfer of the tissue's blood supply, whereas donor-recipient relationship, tissue thickness and donor location describe separate aspects of reconstruction.
metadata.limitation: Original comparison of independently verified definitions, not a copied classification table. It does not claim that perfusion is the sole factor in choosing a reconstruction.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults comparing supplied reconstructive reports.

metadata.statement: Reintroduction of nutrition after starvation shifts metabolism from a predominantly catabolic state toward an anabolic state.
metadata.limitation: Qualitative mechanism background in the observational report; no numerical energy requirement, timing or incidence adopted. The source population is neurocritical care, but only the stated background physiology is used.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing an already evaluated refeeding-related electrolyte course.

metadata.statement: After substantial undernutrition, carbohydrate reintroduction can increase insulin and promote cellular uptake of phosphate, contributing to a fall in serum phosphate during refeeding.
metadata.limitation: The original 2023 cohort report's Introduction is the sole direct mechanism source in this packet. Stable physiology, not its neurocritical risk model or management algorithm. No exact intake, interval, phosphate threshold or claim that every postfeeding fall has this cause.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied compatible outside refeeding course after substantial undernutrition.

metadata.statement: A high-risk nutrition-restart plan includes close clinical and electrolyte monitoring; planned thiamine supplementation does not replace that monitoring.
metadata.limitation: AuSPEN 2025 summary and treatment discussion are the sole direct management source. A qualitative multidisciplinary-care principle, not a bedside feeding protocol or a guarantee of avoiding complications. No monitoring frequency, numeric target, prophylactic electrolyte dose or universal feeding rate.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving an expert-coordinated high-risk nutrition-restart plan.

metadata.statement: A low serum phosphate concentration has causes other than refeeding, so that result alone does not establish refeeding syndrome.
metadata.limitation: AuSPEN 2025 risk and diagnosis discussion supports this limit. No particular diagnostic definition, percentage fall, timing rule or alternative-cause algorithm is adopted. The mechanism cases supply the outside team's assessment and relevant course.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with low phosphate interpreted in a clinical context.

metadata.statement: For adults identified as at risk of refeeding syndrome, the AuSPEN consensus recommends planned thiamine supplementation before restarting nutrition.
metadata.limitation: Single adequate directly verified management source: AuSPEN 2025 section 3.4.1. Expert consensus explicitly reports no specific evidence evaluating thiamine's preventive role; benefit is not guaranteed. Original underlying-fact synthesis under conservative CC BY-NC-ND targeted-verification status. Dose, route, duration, feeding rate and NICE recommendations are excluded.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults already assessed by a specialist nutrition team as at risk during a monitored nutrition restart.

metadata.statement: Healthcare failure mode and effects analysis is a proactive method for identifying potential process failures before those problems occur.
metadata.limitation: Current VA NCPS proactive-risk overview, updated August 28, 2026, supports the healthcare FMEA variant. No claim that every prospective assessment is FMEA, no copied scoring matrix or decision tree, and no statement that the method eliminates risk.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Patients discussing prospective safety review of a planned healthcare process.

metadata.statement: Root cause analysis retrospectively reconstructs an adverse event or close call to identify contributing systems problems, rather than treating individual blame as its central purpose.
metadata.limitation: Current AHRQ primer, reviewed June 15, 2024, directly supports the retrospective systems purpose. This is method classification, not a complete RCA protocol, proof of legal liability, mandated institutional policy or a guarantee of improvement.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Patients discussing an already completed patient-specific safety event.

metadata.statement: Calcineurin phosphatase is the key enzyme inhibited by the tacrolimus–FKBP12 complex in the drug's immunosuppressive mechanism.
metadata.limitation: Exact label section 12.1 supports the principal pathway. This does not assert that tacrolimus has only one molecular interaction or prescribe any change in transplant medicines.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults with specialist-managed tacrolimus immunosuppression.

metadata.statement: Tacrolimus binds the intracellular immunophilin FKBP12; the resulting complex participates in inhibition of calcineurin.
metadata.limitation: Sole direct source is current PROGRAF prescribing information section 12.1. A qualitative mechanism only; no binding affinity, drug-comparison ranking, dose or medication-management rule.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a documented tacrolimus prescription.

metadata.statement: The calcineurin-inhibiting action of tacrolimus suppresses T-lymphocyte activation and proliferation.
metadata.limitation: Sole verified mechanism source is the product label; qualitative immune effect only. No claim of guaranteed rejection prevention, selective depletion of every T cell or control of an individual patient's graft course.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing tacrolimus's immune mechanism.

metadata.statement: A graft transferred between different people who are not genetically identical is an allograft, whether or not they are relatives.
metadata.limitation: Single government dictionary entry supports the relationship; no suitability or immunosuppression recommendation is made.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Human donor-recipient pairs who are not genetically identical.

metadata.statement: A graft transferred from a donor of another species is a xenograft.
metadata.limitation: Relationship only; the scenario supplies an outside-care product record and does not recommend routine animal-organ transplantation.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Recipients of tissue with a supplied different-species origin.

metadata.statement: A graft between genetically identical individuals, such as confirmed monozygotic twins, is an isograft or syngeneic graft.
metadata.limitation: Single government controlled-vocabulary source; twin appearance or a matched blood type alone is not asserted to establish genetic identity.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Genetically identical donor-recipient pairs.

metadata.statement: A graft using tissue obtained from the recipient's own body is an autograft.
metadata.limitation: Donor-recipient terminology only; not a statement about blood supply, rejection, graft survival or the best reconstruction.
metadata.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing documented tissue transplantation.

sourceReviewLimits: Bibliographic and source/claim metadata were independently reviewed during authoring; this native capture verifies actual records and reciprocal claim links, not a new exhaustive source retrieval or named clinician approval.
Medical authority and license/reuse status remain separate in every source record. Government-hosted manufacturer labels are copyrighted targeted verification, not public-domain content.

NHS/OGL, noncommercial/no-derivatives and copyrighted guidance limits remain explicitly recorded. Only independently synthesized underlying facts were used; no source prose, figures, algorithms or original excerpts are retained.

ASA, AAO-HNS AI-prohibited material, NICE restrictions, AAOS limited-use material, RCPI limited-use material and inaccessible primary ACR neck guidance were excluded; derivative reprints were not used as a workaround.

Single-source foundational and management limitations remain explicit at claim level. Older ESGE/WSES criteria, expert-consensus refeeding/thiamine evidence and the educational LAST source retain their recorded dates and certainty limits.

The neck CT task does not assert universal superiority over MRI or ultrasound, and FNA is the best offered initial needle approach with selected core-biopsy alternatives acknowledged. No universal CT-before-FNA sequence is asserted.
All20 groups are unapproved drafts. Agent/editorial/test acceptance is not clinical approval, a public release, therapeutic advice, or proof of owner save or live campaign behavior.
